chapter: Studio notes, hits and old friends
title: Studs Terkel, friend since the Sherman Hotel days
summary: How they met Studs Terkel as emcee, later interviews, and his appearance in Jazz Nativity.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Well at least you don’t do it — or you can’t — but some of the rock ‘n roll guys tune their guitars down a half step so that they can.
Tell the piano player, look could you go tune that thing again. Did you have some association with Studs Turkel?
A dear, sweet friend of ours and a friend of jazz.

Actually, I was the first one to work with him with Charlie Ventura when we did that Sherman Hotel College Union thing, because he was the emcee. Dave Garroway was the emcee for some of the shows, and he alternated when Dave couldn’t make it. And so that’s when we first met him. You met him then too. And then later on we’ve done a lot of interviews with him.

Went up to his studios and did interviews and talked and he would play the current records and so forth. And he would always come in to a club to see us. And let’s see, two years ago, when we did Jazz Nativity at Orchestra Hall in Chicago, Studs took the place of Charles Kuralt and introduced the show. Now for Christmas, Studs came in, came first to see us, his dear friends, we sat in the room and we just talked about old times and this and that. And he was wearing this old raincoat and a great big red scarf around his neck.
A muffler, and this crunched hat. And I said, “well Studs, you’re going to host the show, what are you wearing?” He says, “this is what I’m wearing. I want to look like a caroler.”

He walked out on that stage and the whole audience erupted into applause. It was great. And he’s such a — I really love that guy. He’s so vital and I mean I don’t know how old he is— © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-
He’s in his eighties somewhere. And he’s just so full of life and inspiration, and he’s a very dynamite guy.

And a great writer, great writer, and he’s interested in everything. He’s interested in people, and of course he loved Alec Wilder so the minute we see him we talk about Alec Wilder and all the friends of ours that we have that are mutual friends. Fun.
